attributes.Amenities: BBQ Grill, Pinnacle, Playground, Ethan Allen Tower, Walking Trails, Picnic Table
attributes.Description:
This regional park features acres of natural woodland and the city’s highest point at the top of the Ethan Allen Tower. The 40’ stone tower affords a panoramic view of the city, Lake Champlain, the Green Mountains, and the Adirondacks. Access the park from North Avenue, Ethan Allen Parkway, or the 127 Bike Path. Parking is available at Ethan Allen Park from the park entrance on North Ave. 
 
The Ethan Allen Tower* is open on the following schedule: The tower opens on the second Sunday in May (Mother’s Day) and remains open through October.

From the start of the season until the first day of summer, the tower is generally open only on weekends. For the rest of the season, the tower is open seven days a week.

The tower is open between 9 a.m. and sunset. 
 
*The Tower is opened by volunteers called Tower Keypers. Periodically, something comes up and the tower cannot be opened. Please call 802-864-0123 prior to your visit to confirm that the Tower will be open.

The old forest landscape of the “Arms Grant” rewards visitors with rare natural communities and brims with clues of centuries of land use history. Visitors will find an extensive trail network lined with unusual plants, glimpses of deer and fox, and old farm roads shaded by rich canopies of centurion oaks. A hidden quarry even connects us to a Burlington that was once the national center of marble manufacturing. A rare gem in the necklace of Burlington’s open landscapes, this park is located in the New North End of Burlington.

Arms can be accessed on foot/bike from the Burlington Greenway, with parking available from the end of Kilarney Drive or further away at Leddy Park.

The trailhead into Arthur Park is located next to the bus stop near Burlington High School on the east side North Avenue.

With just one dead end trail, Arthur Park may seem like it does not have much to offer. But to those who plan accordingly, the trail down to Long Pond is a portal to a mysterious cave. By canoe (or foot when the pond has thick enough ice) the rocky recession in cliffs over the pond known as "the Sea Caves" can be seen in all of its splendor. These formations are a remnant of a time when Lake Champlain was much larger and entombed the area in an inland sea.

When the pond freezes over in the winter, BPRW staff and volunteers maintain skating rinks and trails on it's surface.

Crescent Woods' trails can be accessed from Crescent Road via a short set of timber steps that lead down into this forested ravine. The trail network is relatively small and meanders around and over the Englesby Brook.

This hidden gem of an urban wild is tucked carefully in the middle of a neighborhood in the New North End. Although it makes for a short hike, the rare ecosystem affords a contemplative walk over the sometimes dirt, sometimes wood plank trails. Venus Avenue, Red Maple Lane, and the corner of Sunset Drive and Meridian Street each have informal trailheads to this land of tall trees and fern filled bogs.

McKenzie Park’s rare sandy shores, cathedral-like riverside woods, and historic farmlands are an ideal place to retire from the hustle-and-bustle of downtown Burlington. 

McKenzie Park is only accessible via foot or bike along trails connecting to the Intervale Center, Ethan Allen Homestead, and the 127 Bike Path.

attributes.Amenities: Basketball Court, BBQ Grill, Beach, Bike Path Accessible, Ice Arena, Mountain Bike Park, Tennis Court, Pickleball, Picnic Pavilion, Soccer Field, Softball Diamond, Walking Trails, Indoor Ice Arena, Outdoor Fitness Station
attributes.Description:
Leddy is a large regional park that contains multiple athletic fields, playing courts, a large beach, the Gordon H Paquette Ice Arena, and expansive woodlands with a network of gently-sloped trails. Public restrooms within the ice arena are open year round. A tent is erected seasonally between the beach and ice arena that can be rented for community gatherings.

The park can be accessed from the Burlington Greenway, which passes through the western portion of the park, and along Leddy Park Road, which intersects with North Avenue. A large parking area is located just uphill and east of the Ice Arena and a smaller parking area is located nearby the athletic courts and soccer fields in the east end of the park.

attributes.Amenities: Bike Path Accessible, Community Garden, Dog Park, Soccer Field, Playground, Outdoor Ice Rink, Outdoor Fitness Station
attributes.Description:
Starr Farm Park features athletic fields, a large dog park, community gardens, a playground, and outdoor exercise equipment. The Burlington Greenway runs the length of the Park and splits it into two separate parts. When winter weather permits, BPRW Staff maintain a large outdoor ice rink in the Park's southeast corner.

The Park can also be accessed via Starr Farm Rd, with three separate gravel parking areas for the gardens, dog park, and playground/sports fields.

attributes.Amenities: BBQ Grill, Bike Path Accessible, Picnic Pavilion, Picnic Table, Playground, SUP & Kayak Rental, Campground
attributes.Description:
North Beach is our largest beach. With food concessions, a playground, restrooms with showers, picnic tables and grills, North Beach has something for everyone! During the summer months you can also rent kayaks, canoes and stand up paddleboards from local vendors. 

The park and beach are open and accessible by bike or foot all year, though only seasonally accessible by car between May and October. The Park can be accessed via Institute Road from North Ave or from the Burlington Greenway. 

North Beach also boasts a campground with sites available for overnight rentals. Rentals may be booked online through our website.

If you have questions about the Beach or Campground, please call (802)862-0942 or email NBCampground@burlingtonvt.gov

This natural area is only accessible by staircases from the Burlington Greenway. Parking is available nearby at Starr Farm Park. The area provides access to Lake Champlain and is a popular spot for quiet sunsets.

Northshore Natural Area is not one of our dedicated swimming beaches. There are no lifeguards and, because there is no stable access for equipment, the beach cannot be groomed by our staff.
A small, ungroomed beach that can only be accessed on bike or foot via the Burlington Greenway.

attributes.Amenities: Basketball Court, Community Garden, Picnic Table, Playground
attributes.Description:
Baird Park is a small neighborhood park in Burlington’s south end and is accessed from Pine St. and the adjacent Southcrest neighborhood.

The park features a playground, community gardens, a basketball court, and a small open lawn.

attributes.Amenities: Accessible Treehouse, BBQ Grill, Beach, Bike Path Accessible, Bocce, Outdoor Fitness, Outdoor Tennis Court, Picnic Pavilion, Picnic Table, Playground, SUP & Kayak Rental, Volleyball Courts, Walking Trails
attributes.Description:
Oakledge Park is located in the South End of Burlington along the shores of Lake Champlain, allowing for beautiful waterfront and sunset views. 

It is home to two beaches – Blanchard Beach and The Cove. There are two large shelters that are available to rent (see our rentals page for details), a universally accessible playground, the "world’s first accessible tree house," walking trails, tennis, bocce and volleyball courts, charcoal grills, picnic tables, bathrooms and lots of open grassy areas for you to enjoy.

Oakledge is located at the end of Flynn Avenue and has two dedicated parking areas (though the lots tend to fill up quickly during the summer). It can also be reached by bike or foot from the Burlington Greenway, which runs the length of the Park.

attributes.Amenities: BBQ Grill, Beach, Picnic Pavilion, Picnic Table, Playground, SUP Rentals, Bike Path Accessible
attributes.Description: The beautiful sandy Blanchard Beach is located just off the end of Flynn Avenue, nestled within Oakledge Park. There is no lifeguard coverage at Blanchard Beach. Available facilities at Oakledge Park include tennis courts, bocce courts, volleyball courts, two picnic shelters, a universally accessible playground, walking trails, and public restrooms. The park and beach are open all year, the uninsulated restrooms are closed seasonally.

attributes.Amenities: Basketball Court, Playground, Bike Path Accessible, Outdoor Ice Rink
attributes.Description:
Lakeside Park lies at the heart of the neighborhood that bears its name. Occupying 2/3 of a city block surrounded by Central Ave., Conger Ave., and Harrison Ave. The on-street section of the Burlington Greenway runs along the southern edge of the Park.

The neighborhood operates an outdoor ice rink at Lakeside Park when winter weather permits.

attributes.Amenities: Baseball Diamond, Basketball Court, Community Garden, Pickleball, Playground, Soccer Field, Tennis Court, Outdoor Ice Rink, Sledding Hill
attributes.Description:
Situated on a hillside between two well-known residential neighborhoods (Five Sisters & Birchcliff), Calahan is a regional hub for soccer and baseball leagues, and an important park for the surrounding neighborhoods.

During the winter, the community maintains an outdoor ice rink in the park and the hillsides provide some of the best sledding opportunities in the City.

attributes.Amenities: Softball Diamond, Basketball Court, Natural Playground
attributes.Description: Smalley Park, a neighborhood park just south of downtown, is home to the city’s only natural playground, in addition to active recreation facilities. The park can be accessed via Adams & St. Paul Streets, and from the end of Elm Terrace.

attributes.Amenities: Bike Path Accessible, Picnic Table, Playground, Marina
attributes.Description:
Perkins Pier lies right along the Burlington Greenway Bike Path and at the Western end of Maple Street. This waterfront park offers a playground, seasonal restrooms and quiet benches overlooking the Burlington harbor. 

The park is home to one of Burlington's City-operated Marinas and contains a large gravel parking lot that is easily accessible from Burlington's Downtown.
Located near Perkins Pier right along the Burlington Greenway Bike Path, this waterfront park hosts local scupltures and quiet benches for taking in the sunset across Lake Champlain.

City Hall Park is an urban park located in the heart of downtown Burlington, surrounded by College, St. Paul and Main Streets and immediately adjacent to the Church St. Marketplace, Burlington City Arts (BCA), and Burlington's City Hall.

A central splashpad/fountain operates from approximately 9am to 10:30pm in the warmer months. It will automatically shut off if winds exceed 12mph or when raining and occasionally for maintenance and closes for the winter season on October 12. Tables and chairs are put out as weather and staffing capacity permit.

BCA hosts music, performance, and vending events in the park during various times throughout the year.

The Portland Loo restroom located in the park is open seasonally. Year-round restrooms located on the ground floor of City Hall can be accessed from the Church St. entrance.

Free Wi-Fi is made available in the Park by Burlington Telecom.

attributes.Amenities: Bandshell, Playground, Picnic Table, Outdoor Rink, Art/Sculpture
attributes.Description:
Located on a high point overlooking Waterfront Park, Lake Champlain and the distant Adirondack mountains, Battery Park is located on the western edge of downtown. Accessed from Battery, College and Sherman Streets, this historic park provides a panoramic view of Lake Champlain and the Adirondacks with a promenade, playground, monuments, and a bandshell. 

The park bandshell periodically hosts concerts during the summer. The park and bandshell are available to rent through our website.

The Battery Park Extension, runs from the southern end of Battery Park at Pearl Street south to College Street. The extension includes several marble art pieces as well as a memorial fountain and plaza dedicated to Burlington architect and Chamber of Commerce President, Robert A. Metz.

There is a small parking area located along the north side of the Park, accessible from Sherman St.

Waterfront Park is a large regional park located to the west of downtown along Lake Champlain, with the Burlington Greenway running along its eastern side. The event lawn at the north end of the park hosts several large music and food festivals in the summer. 

The park is adjacent to the Burlington Community Boathouse and Marina, the ECHO Museum, Waterworks Park, the Moran FRAME, and the Lake Champlain Sailing Center. The park can be accessed via College & Lake Streets and Penny Lane.

Year-round restrooms are located inside the ECHO Center and at the Burlington Community Sailing Center. Seasonal restrooms are located at the Pease lot info center, the Burlington Community Boathouse, and the Burlington Harbor Marina.

Parking is available at the Pease lot located at the Bottom of College Street, and at the northern lots along Lake Street and Penny Lane near the Skatepark.

attributes.Amenities: Fishing, Walking Trails, Boardwalk, Bike Path Accessible
attributes.Description:
Located at the end of Penny Lane north of Waterfront Park and tucked away behind Burlington's Water Treatment Plant, Water Works Park includes a wooden boardwalk, walking paths, large garden beds planted with native trees and shrubs, benches, and a small lawn. Food trucks often operate out of the Park in the summer.

The Burlington Fishing Pier and the Moran FRAME can be accessed from the walkways in the Park. There is a limited amount of parking available with additional parking located nearby along Lake St and Penny Lane.

Seasonal restrooms are located just south of the park at the Burlington Harbor Marina.
A small neighborhood park in the Old North End, Pomeroy park is surrounded by residences on Booth and North Streets. Pomeroy is famous for its pickup basketball and features a small playground.

attributes.Amenities: Basketball Court, Pickleball, Playground, Softball Field, Tennis Court, Takraw Court
attributes.Description:
Schmanska Park is located in the east end of Burlington, near the City borders with Winooski and South Burlington. The park contains an open field, a combined tennis-pickleball-takraw court, a basketball court, a playground, and a red barn that can be rented  for community meetings and events

The park can be accessed from Gove Ct, which runs between the park and it's dedicated parking area.

attributes.Amenities: Baseball Diamond, Basketball Court, Pickleball, Playground, Tennis Court, Soccer Field, Outdoor Ice Rink
attributes.Description:
Roosevelt Park is the heart and soul of the Old North End and functions as both a neighborhood park and home to organized baseball and soccer leagues. In 2014, the Burlington Boys & Girls Club’s renovated the former warming shelter for use as their Academic Teen Center. 

The park is surrounded by Oak, Willow, Walnut and St. Mary Streets. Nearby ‘Little Rosie’ contains a children’s playground.

When winter weather permits, BPRW Staff maintain an outdoor ice rink at the park.

Dewey Park is a small community park located between Spring, Archibald and Walnut Streets. 

The park hosts the ONE Farmer’s Market on Tuesdays from 3-6 pm, June – October.

In 2014, a traffic calming project closed a section of Spring Street and reclaimed the space for recreation. The area features a street mural designed and executed by artist Abby Manock, vegetation planted and maintained by community volunteers, Monkton Quartzite boulders, and movable furniture  made available during the farmers market and special events.

in 2024, the 18-foot tall Embrace and Belonging Monument, created by artist Ai Qiu Hopen, was installed in the Park

This mini park at the intersections of North Winooski Street and Archibald Street provides a shady grassy area. The park was named for George and Elaine Little in 1996 as a dedication of their service to Burlington's community.

attributes.Amenities: Baseball Diamond, Basketball Court, Playground, Tennis Court
attributes.Description: Appletree Park is a neighborhood park with two tennis courts, two basketball courts, a playground, and a youth ball field.

Elmwood Cemetery is located at the corner of Elmwood Avenue and North Street in the City’s Old North End. The cemetery contains the graves of Ethan Allen’s second wife, Frances “Fanny” Montresor Penniman, naturalist Zadock Thompson, pilot Joseph Barron of MacDonought’s flagship "The Saratoga" at the Battle of Plattsburgh, revolutionary war soldiers and many early residents of the City.

Space is not available for any additional burials. Open by request. Call 863-2075 to make arrangements.

attributes.Amenities: Baseball Diamond, Disc Golf, Softball Diamond
attributes.Description:
Schifilliti Park mainly serves as a Little League hub and home to a 9-hole disc golf course. The Park lies between athletic facilities at Hunt Middle School & CP Smith Elementary School. and is immediately adjacent to the BPRW Miller Community & Recreation Center. 

Year-round public restrooms located in the Miller Center are open during the Miller Center's open hours. Seasonal restrooms in the Little League snack shack are open during little league events.

Access is via Gosse Ct.or by foot or bike from either school.
A small urban park in a growing section of downtown, featuring a playground, picnic tables, and a small lawn.
This historic cemetery contains the final resting place for Ethan Allen and a number of his family members. Space is not available for any additional burials.

attributes.Amenities: Beach, Bike Path Accessible, Dog Park
attributes.Description: “Texaco Beach” is the City’s only dedicated Dog Beach providing water access to canines year-round. The beach is conveniently located near the Waterfront Dog Park with access off of the Burlington Greenway from the Urban Reserve.

Lakeview Cemetery is an example of a Victorian Lawn Park Cemetery and was first opened to the public in 1872. It contains the Louisa Howard Chapel that was built in 1882 and was a gift to the City from Louisa Howard. 

The Chapel (which was entered into the National Register of Historic Places in 1999) is available to rent for memorial services, weddings and other public gatherings.

attributes.Amenities: Indoor Gym, Community Center, Basketball Court, Outdoor Fitness Station
attributes.Description:
The Miller Center, opened in 2008, hosts programs for a variety of ages and interests and offers space for community meetings, workshops, conferences, parties, athletic events and much more. We also welcome suggestions for new programs!

The Miller Center is also home to Frog & Toad Childcare & Learning Center.  The Miller Center offers free Wi-Fi through Burlington Telecom and plenty of free parking. The center is accessible by bike or foot from the surrounding neighborhoods and is located at the east end of Gosse Ct.

This mini park at the intersection of St. Paul Street and South Winooski Avenue offers a quiet seating area amidst the bustle of busy streets.

Potvin Park was named after Bob & Judy Potvin who lived next door and meticulously maintained it for many years.

attributes.Amenities: Community Garden, Walking Trails, Picnic Table, Bike Path Accessible
attributes.Description:
Kieslich Park is home to the Lakeview Community Garden, walking trails, and BPRW's Conservation Team. 

The Red Stone Cottage at the parks entrance from North Ave. is currently used as office space by the Conservation Team and contains publicly accessible restrooms.

A steep dirt trail currently crosses the Park connecting from the Burlington Greenway to North Avenue. Future plans call for paving and regrading the pathway.

attributes.Amenities: BBQ Grill, Beach, Bike Path Accessible, Picnic Pavilion, Picnic Table, Walking Trails
attributes.Description: Oakledge Cove is our most secluded public beach. The area features scenic rocky outcroppings and is a popular spot for quiet sunsets. The Cove is located near the Upper Shelter and restrooms at Oakledge Park, and is easily accessed via the bike path. There is a grassy area adjacent to the beach that is ideal for picnics and BBQs. The park and beach are open all year.

Leddy Park boasts a 1500′ sandy beach overlooked by a grassy picnic area with grills and picnic tables. Restrooms are available inside the Gordon H. Paquette Ice Arena. There is no lifeguard coverage.

The Gordon H. Paquette Ice Arena at Leddy Park is a full service arena with a “Standard” rink (200×85) and a versatile “Studio” rink (87×66, available mid-September through March).

Please see our rentals page for information regarding pricing and reservations.

Nestled on the shores of beautiful Lake Champlain, in almost 45 acres of woods and beach, lies one of Burlington’s hidden treasures — North Beach Campground — an urban campground with a decidedly rural character.

There are 137 great sites to either pitch your tent or park your RV or trailer. With its premier natural sand beach, shaded campsites and picnic grounds, North Beach offers an incomparable experience for anyone wishing to camp in Vermont.

The campground is open May 15 through October 15.Rentals may be booked online through our website.

If you have questions about the Beach or Campground, please call (802)862-0942 or email NBCampground@burlingtonvt.gov

Burlington is home to a world class concrete Skatepark, featuring bowls, pools, metal grind rails, boxes and ramps of all shapes and sizes. Dedicated to local legend and DJ Andy A_Dog Williams on June 4, 2016, the site is adjacent to the Burlington Greenway and waterfront parking lots. 

Public restrooms are located just north of the skate park at the Burlington Community Sailing Center.

The Waterfront Dog Park is located along the Burlington Greenway a short walk north of the Burlington Community Sailing Center and A_Dog Skatepark and a short walk south of the nearby Texaco Dog Beach. The Park consists of a nearly 2-acre fenced in dog run with a "small dog area" in it's northeast corner.

Starr Farm Dog Park provides nearly 3-and-a-half acres of fenced in area for your dog to run and socialize with other dogs, with a "small dog area" set aside in its southwest corner. A water spigot is turned on seasonally in the summer to fill a small pool and drinking bowls. 

There is a small gravel parking lot at the south end of the dog park that can be accessed from Starr Farm Road and both of the Dog Parks entrances are easily accessible from the Burlington Greenway.

The Community Boathouse Marina offers transient dockage, services, public access to views, and a fantastic, dockside restaurant, Splash at the Boathouse. Find hourly dockage, moorings or overnight dockage with access to shopping, amenities, and fantastic restaurants all within walking distance.

Come pull up a seat in one of our Adirondack chairs located on our fully public dock and enjoy the best view in town!
